TERROR XIX's Rotary Motor is equipped with a two-way relief valve that serves as a brake valve and protects the rotary motor from excessive instantaneous back pressure. Hydraulic control provides smoother and more precise flow output, enabling stable climbing and descent on slopes through fine adjustments. The new hydraulic foot pedal for auxiliary functions (e.g., breaker) allows for convenient control of the attachment while simultaneously operating the boom and arm. The leftmost pedal controls the breaker, while the rightmost is a spare.

Boom Swing. The left and right deflection angles of 45 degrees adds extra agility to the machine.

This upgraded hydraulic operation offers greater convenience and flexibility, enabling the operator to adjust the blade height while simultaneously traveling.

Retractable Tracks with a retractable range of 1-1.16m allow for ease of navigation on narrow paths.

An upgraded triple hydraulic pump that allows the hydraulic flow to be 15% faster than those on other two ton excavators. The increase in hydraulic flow can increase the working speed and more operations more efficient.

Three way stop valve. These valves are used to add a hydraulic function, such as an auger or thumb attachment, by rerouting the flow from an existing hydraulic line

Hidden single speed motor use a single-speed final drive motor assembly that is typically built into the sprocket. This design provides a more compact profile and can offer smoother travel. Single-speed models are best for applications where constant, controlled speed is more important than rapid travel.

The piston travel motor offers a volumetric efficiency and service life that are 3 to 5 times greater than those of standard motors. It also provides a 30% increase in output torque, resulting in superior extrication capability and enhanced mobility between worksites. As the piston motor is embedded within the undercarriage, it is effectively protected from impacts and debris during travel and operation.
